Never done this before?

Three steps. That is the whole thing.Cách Ăn Lẩu

Hot pot looks intimidating from the outside. It is not. Your server walks you through it, and you are cooking within five minutes of sitting down.

1

Pick your broth

Your server runs through the options. Rich and porky, clean chicken, sour and spicy Thai, numbing Sichuan, kimchi, or an all vegetable pot. Not sure? Ask. They will steer you right.

2

Grab off the belt

Fresh plates ride past your seat under clear lids, every one labelled. Take whatever looks good. Meat, seafood, greens, mushrooms, noodles, dumplings. Keep taking.

3

Cook and eat

Your pot sits on a burner built into the table. Give it three to five minutes to come to a boil, then drop things in. Thin meat takes seconds. Take your time.

Why "Rotary"

The food comes to you.

Most hot pot restaurants hand you a checklist and a pencil. We run a conveyor belt around the dining room, stacked with fresh plates under clear lids. You see the food before you commit to it, and you never wait on a kitchen.

Every seat gets its own pot and its own burner, so nobody has to agree on a broth. Order what you want, cook it how you like it, at your own speed.

It is a genuinely fun way to eat dinner, and it is the reason people bring out of town guests here.

First time? Read this

How to eat hot pot.Cách Ăn Lẩu

Nobody is born knowing how to do this. Here is the whole thing, start to finish, so you can walk in already knowing what happens.

1

Pick your broth

A server will ask what broth you want and walk you through the options. There is no wrong answer, and there is no shame in asking what something tastes like. That is what they are there for.

2

Pick your food

Fresh plates ride past your seat on the belt, each one under a clear lid and labelled, so you always know what you are grabbing. Take a plate. Take six. Keep going as long as you are hungry.

3

Wait, then cook

Your server sets your pot on the burner in front of you and shows you how it works. Give it three to five minutes to come to a rolling boil, then start dropping food in and building your own pot.

The small print

Things worth knowing before you sit down.

Everyone gets their own pot. You do not have to negotiate a broth with the rest of your table. Order the one you want.

Thin meat cooks fast. Sliced beef and lamb need a few seconds in a rolling boil, not a few minutes. Dumplings, root vegetables and corn take longer.

Take it slow. There is no rush and no set course order. Cook a little, eat it, go back for more.

Tell us about allergies and diets. Because you pick every ingredient yourself, hot pot is one of the easiest meals to eat around a restriction. Vegetarians can order the vegetable broth and stay entirely in the vegetable, tofu, mushroom and noodle plates.

Our story

There is no sincerer love than the love of food.

A dining room built around a simple idea. Give people good ingredients, a pot of boiling broth, and let them cook their own dinner.

What hot pot is

Dinner cooked at the table, not in a kitchen.

Hot pot is an East Asian way of eating: a simmering pot of stock set right on your table, and a spread of raw ingredients you cook in it yourself, a few pieces at a time.

There are three parts to it. The broth you cook in. The ingredients you dip. The sauce you dip them into afterwards. Everything else is up to you.

It is also, quietly, one of the healthier ways to eat out. Nothing is deep fried or drowned in sauce before it reaches you. It is vegetables, mushrooms, seafood and thin cut meat, cooked in broth, seasoned by you.

What makes us different

We did not pick one country.

Most hot pot restaurants commit to a single tradition and cook within it. We did the opposite. Our broths come from across Asia: Vietnam, China, Thailand, Korea and beyond, sitting on the same menu.

Then there is the belt. Instead of a checklist and a pencil, we run a conveyor around the dining room stacked with fresh plates under clear lids. You see the food before you take it. Nothing waits on a kitchen.

And every seat gets its own pot and its own burner, which means a table of six can eat six different dinners without anybody compromising.

When we opened, there was nothing else like it in the Seattle area.
